fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions on the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with posts or reflective stakes to help responders locate the access point at night or in smoke conditions.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles to allow fire apparatus and emergency vehicles to reach the residence.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain vehicle clearance for large emergency equipment.
• Cut back trees and shrubs overhanging the access drive to allow ladder trucks and tall apparatus to pass without obstruction.
• Clear a flat, stable area near the residence where emergency vehicles can turn around, and keep it free of stored equipment, vehicles, and debris.
• Mark any turnaround area with low stakes or painted curbing so its boundaries are visible to drivers unfamiliar with the property.
• Thin dense vegetation between the access drive and the detached structure so responders on foot can move between the two buildings.
• Keep a clear walking path between the main residence and the detached structure free of overgrown shrubs and debris.
• Post the property address on the detached structure if it is set back from the main residence and not visible from the access drive.
• Install a gate lock box or leave the gate consistently unlocked if a gate restricts access on the single entry drive.
• Notify your local fire department of the single

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches and shrubs that are directly touching or overhanging the roof and exterior walls.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest the structure to create open space between individual trees and between the trees and the house.
• Remove shrubs and low brush growing directly against the foundation and exterior walls on all sides of the structure.
• Clear ground vegetation within the immediate area around the structure, keeping it short and sparse close to the walls.
• Separate shrubs and scattered trees by removing or cutting back plants that form a continuous path of vegetation from the surrounding area to the structure.
• Thin scattered trees and shrubs along the single access driveway so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep overhanging branches trimmed back above the driveway to maintain clear vehicle height along the full length of the route.
• Remove brush and dense vegetation from the edges of the driveway to keep the travel surface and shoulders visible and passable.
• Clear dead plant material, fallen branches, and leaf litter from around the base of trees and shrubs near the structure.
• Thin vegetation in the brush area closest to the structure to open up space between that area and the building.
• Remove or cut back mixed vegetation on the sides of the structure where separation between plants and the walls is smallest.
• Keep the area immediately surrounding the structure mowed short and free of accumulated dry plant material.
